skill.name: gaffa-authoring
skill.description: Write, edit, review, and migrate browser automation code for the Gaffa REST API using action references, request templates, and live documentation.
skill.summary: Author Gaffa API workflows for page capture, structured extraction, pagination, and bounded asynchronous polling.
skill.author: gaffaai

security_audit.summary: All 132 static findings are false positives for the reported threats: Markdown formatting, API identifiers, documented network operations, and credential protection explain the matches. A separate consent risk remains because code-authoring requests trigger paid third-party page capture without an explicit authorization checkpoint. No evidence found of malware, credential theft, or instructions to manipulate this audit.

remediation.issue: Installation is treated as consent for Gaffa processing, and extraction authoring requires a live page capture before code generation.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for the provider, target URL, external processing, and charges before live capture. Offer code-only authoring with supplied markup or explicitly unverified selectors.

semantic_findings.title: Paid third-party capture without explicit consent
semantic_findings.description: The skill treats installation as consent to use Gaffa for generic scraping requests. It requires live page capture before writing extraction code, potentially disclosing target URLs and processing page content externally while consuming credits without execution approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly require Gaffa page capture before extraction authoring and infer provider selection from installation. No explicit approval checkpoint separates code generation from billed external processing.

content.value_statement: Browser automation integrations require accurate request fields, selectors, and polling logic. This skill guides Gaffa API code authoring with action references, live documentation, and adaptable templates.
actual_capabilities: Guide synchronous and asynchronous browser requests with explicit runtime limits, bounded polling, and error handling.
Select deterministic extraction methods for tables, repeated items, and individual elements.
Design inline extraction schemas and reusable schemas for the parse_json action.
Map Playwright, Puppeteer, and Selenium workflows to Gaffa browser actions and pagination loops.
Guide screenshot, DOM, Markdown, PDF, cookie, and file capture using documented action parameters.
Apply environment-based authentication, output redaction, and recording controls in generated workflows.
limitations: Live execution requires Gaffa access and an API key; default residential proxies require a paid account and incur bandwidth charges.
Each browser request starts a fresh session, so session state does not persist across separate requests.
Synchronous requests have a 60-second cap; asynchronous limits depend on the account plan.
LLM-backed extraction can vary between runs, and live documentation or target-page access may be unavailable.

use_cases.description: Choose table parsing or a single container capture, then produce structured product fields with explicit runtime and polling limits.

use_cases.description: Author screenshot or PDF capture requests with suitable waits, scrolling, output handling, and recording controls.

prompt_templates.title: Build asynchronous pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an asynchronous Gaffa workflow for [URL] in [language]. Capture each page before clicking next, bound polling, handle failures, and confirm paid execution first.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a browser script
prompt_templates.prompt: Port this [Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium] script to Gaffa: [script]. Preserve outputs, identify session limitations, and justify any LLM extraction. Request approval before execution.

output_examples.input: Draft a workflow that extracts prices from a standard HTML table.
output: Recommended approach: use table parsing after confirming the table selector with approved page inspection.
Convert returned price strings into numeric values in the client script.
Use bounded asynchronous polling and report action failures separately from successful completion.

output_examples.input: Review a migration that logs in once and reuses the session across separate requests.
output: Migration constraint: Gaffa starts a fresh browser session for every request.
Keep dependent interactions within one request where supported, or redesign the workflow.
Treat captured cookies as credentials and keep request recordings disabled outside approved debugging.

best_practices: Approve the provider, target URLs, external processing, and expected charges before running live captures.
Inspect approved page markup before choosing selectors, and prefer deterministic extraction when the structure is stable.
Keep credentials in the environment, redact outputs, and bound browser execution and polling with explicit limits.
anti_patterns: Running paid third-party requests when the user requested only code or design advice.
Using LLM extraction for fixed rules or stable tables that deterministic parsing can handle.
Assuming sessions persist across requests or allowing polling to continue without a deadline.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Live workflows also need suitable HTTP or documentation tool access.

faq.question: Do I need a Gaffa account and API key?
faq.answer: Live API requests require a Gaffa key provided through GAFFA_API_KEY. The skill does not include credentials.

faq.question: Does the skill include an SDK?
faq.answer: No SDK is bundled. It provides Markdown guidance and curl templates that the assistant adapts to your language and HTTP library.

faq.question: Does every extraction use an LLM?
faq.answer: No. The guidance prefers deterministic table parsing or captured HTML for stable structures. The parse_json action supports variable or interpretive content.

faq.question: Can browser sessions persist across requests?
faq.answer: No. Each request starts a fresh session. Supported repeated interactions can use the loop action within one request.

faq.question: Can authoring trigger network requests or charges?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow calls for live documentation lookup and Gaffa page inspection before extraction code. Require approval for external processing and charges first.
